part.name: Splined sprocket assembly
part.description: Two-solid, thin annular power-transmission model comprising a large 27-tooth sprocket body with a lightweight spoke/web structure and a separate central internally splined insert. The solids are coaxially nested but remain distinct B-rep solids, indicating separate functional components rather than accidental disconnected geometry.
part.symmetry_note: Both solids are organized around the common thin-part axis, geometrically corresponding to the CAD Y direction. SOLID 0 has a repeated internal spline profile. SOLID 1 has a 27-member circular tooth pattern and an approximately circular repeated spoke/cutout network. The overall body is approximately rotationally periodic, although the spoke openings vary in shape.

semantic_orientation.description: The object is a rotational power-transmission component, so top, bottom, left, and right are not intrinsic semantic sides. The two broad axial faces can reasonably be called front and back, but their assignment to the labeled face-on views remains interpretation rather than geometric fact. The functional rotation axis is the thin-part axis, corresponding to CAD Y in the STEP geometry.

part.name: Splined sprocket assembly
part.description: Two-solid, thin annular power-transmission model comprising a large 27-tooth sprocket body with a lightweight spoke/web structure and a separate central internally splined insert. The solids are coaxially nested but remain distinct B-rep solids, indicating separate functional components rather than accidental disconnected geometry.
part.symmetry_note: Both solids are organized around the common thin-part axis, geometrically corresponding to the CAD Y direction. SOLID 0 has a repeated internal spline profile. SOLID 1 has a 27-member circular tooth pattern and an approximately circular repeated spoke/cutout network. The overall body is approximately rotationally periodic, although the spoke openings vary in shape.

semantic_orientation.description: The object is a rotational power-transmission component, so top, bottom, left, and right are not intrinsic semantic sides. The two broad axial faces can reasonably be called front and back, but their assignment to the labeled face-on views remains interpretation rather than geometric fact. The functional rotation axis is the thin-part axis, corresponding to CAD Y in the STEP geometry.
